difficultyReason: The stimulus presents mixed quantitative data with an important qualification about a subgroup. The correct answer respects a hedged qualification that several trap answers either drop or invert. Test-takers must identify the modest inference that survives the stated exception.
stimulus: A survey of 1,200 adults conducted by a public health institute found that people who reported sleeping fewer than six hours per night were approximately twice as likely to report persistent fatigue during daytime hours as those sleeping seven or more hours. However, among adults who engaged in vigorous aerobic exercise at least four times per week, the association between short sleep duration and daytime fatigue was substantially weaker — short-sleeping exercisers reported daytime fatigue at only a slightly elevated rate compared to well-rested non-exercisers. Adults in the survey who both slept fewer than six hours and did not exercise regularly reported the highest rates of daytime fatigue of any group. The survey did not assess diet or caffeine intake.
questionStem: The statements above, if true, most support which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Regular vigorous exercise eliminates the negative effects of insufficient sleep on daytime energy levels.

choices.label: B
choices.text: For at least some adults, engaging in regular vigorous exercise may reduce, though not necessarily eliminate, fatigue associated with sleeping fewer than six hours per night.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Adults who sleep fewer than six hours per night will experience persistent daytime fatigue regardless of their exercise habits.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Insufficient sleep is a less significant contributor to daytime fatigue than a sedentary lifestyle.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Caffeine intake is the primary reason that some short-sleeping exercisers avoid persistent daytime fatigue.

explanations.correct: The survey shows that among short-sleeping adults who exercise vigorously, daytime fatigue rates were only slightly elevated compared to well-rested non-exercisers — substantially weaker than the general short-sleep association. This supports a hedged inference that regular exercise may reduce (but not necessarily eliminate) fatigue for at least some short sleepers. The language 'at least some' and 'may reduce' correctly respects both the positive finding and the absence of certainty.
explanations.A: Too strong. The stimulus says the association was 'substantially weaker,' not absent. 'Eliminates' overclaims the effect.
explanations.C: Opposite direction. The data specifically show that short-sleeping exercisers do NOT report the same high rates as short-sleeping non-exercisers, directly contradicting this absolute claim.
explanations.D: Relative/absolute confusion and scope creep. The stimulus compares subgroups of short sleepers, not sleep versus exercise as independent variables across the full population. No such ranking of contributors is established.
explanations.E: Plausible but unsupported. The stimulus explicitly states that caffeine intake was not assessed, so no inference about caffeine's role can be drawn from these data.

difficultyReason: The stimulus contains economic data with a counterintuitive finding about a specific industry subgroup. Trap answers include a too-strong absolute claim, a scope-creep answer that generalizes beyond the stated data, and a plausible-but-unsupported causal explanation. Test-takers must isolate the modest comparative inference the data actually license.
stimulus: Data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics covering the period from 2010 to 2022 show that, in the United States, wages in the software development sector rose by an average of 34 percent in inflation-adjusted terms, while wages across all private-sector occupations rose by an average of 8 percent over the same period. Yet among software developers employed at firms with fewer than ten employees, inflation-adjusted wages rose by only 11 percent — barely above the all-sector average. Firms with more than 500 employees in the software sector accounted for the majority of the outsized wage growth. The data do not include freelance or contract workers.
questionStem: Which one of the following is most strongly supported by the information above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Software developers at large firms earned more in absolute terms than software developers at small firms throughout the period from 2010 to 2022.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The overall wage growth in the software sector during this period was driven largely by wage increases at large firms rather than small ones.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Software developers who work as freelancers experienced wage growth comparable to that of developers at large firms.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Employees at small software firms would have seen higher wage growth had they moved to larger firms during this period.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The wage premium enjoyed by large-firm software developers reflects their superior technical skills compared to small-firm developers.

explanations.correct: The stimulus states that large firms (500+ employees) accounted for the majority of the outsized wage growth in the software sector, while small firms saw growth barely above the all-sector average. This directly and strongly supports the inference that the sector-wide figure was driven primarily by large-firm wage increases.
explanations.A: Relative/absolute confusion. The data describe rates of wage growth, not absolute wage levels. Nothing in the stimulus establishes which group earned more in absolute dollars at any point.
explanations.C: Plausible but unsupported. The stimulus explicitly excludes freelance and contract workers from the dataset, so no inference about their wages is warranted.
explanations.D: Scope creep and unsupported counterfactual. The data describe aggregate trends, not the outcomes that individual workers would have experienced by switching employers. No basis exists for this individual-level causal claim.
explanations.E: Plausible but unsupported. The stimulus offers no information about the skills or qualifications of developers at different firm sizes; attributing the differential to skill differences introduces an explanation the data do not address.

difficultyReason: The environmental science stimulus presents data about a counterintuitive trend in a specific ecosystem, with a qualification that limits the scope of any inference. Trap answers include one that generalizes to all ecosystems (scope creep), one that inverts the finding, one that introduces an unsupported causal mechanism, and one using absolute language the data do not warrant.
stimulus: Ecologists monitoring a temperate coastal wetland over a 15-year period documented a steady increase in overall plant species diversity, despite a concurrent rise in average water salinity attributed to reduced freshwater inflow. Closer analysis revealed that this diversity increase was confined almost entirely to a narrow transitional zone at the wetland's inland edge, where salt-tolerant species were colonizing areas previously dominated by a single freshwater sedge. In the wetland's central and seaward zones, species diversity either held steady or declined slightly over the same period. The ecologists noted that similar long-term salinity data were not available for comparable wetlands in the region.
questionStem: The information above most strongly supports which one of the following claims?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rising salinity in coastal wetlands generally promotes plant species diversity by enabling salt-tolerant species to colonize new areas.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The freshwater sedge that previously dominated the transitional zone was probably less salt-tolerant than the species that replaced it.

choices.label: C
choices.text: In the wetland studied, the overall increase in plant species diversity masked divergent trends in different zones of the wetland.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Reduced freshwater inflow will ultimately eliminate plant diversity in the central and seaward zones of the wetland.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Salt-tolerant plant species are more resilient than freshwater species and will eventually dominate all zones of this wetland.

explanations.correct: The stimulus explicitly shows that the wetland's overall diversity increase was driven entirely by the transitional zone, while the central and seaward zones held steady or declined slightly. This directly supports the inference that the aggregate figure concealed divergent zone-level trends — an inference that follows cleanly from the data without overclaiming.
explanations.A: Scope creep. The data concern a single wetland over 15 years, and the ecologists explicitly note that comparable data from other wetlands are unavailable. Generalizing to 'coastal wetlands generally' goes well beyond what the evidence supports.
explanations.B: Plausible but unsupported. While this is a biologically reasonable hypothesis, the stimulus describes colonization patterns but never compares the salt tolerance of the displaced sedge to the colonizing species. This is an appealing worldly inference not grounded in the stated facts.
explanations.D: Too strong and opposite direction on certainty. The data show slight or stable trends in those zones, not a trajectory toward elimination. 'Will ultimately eliminate' introduces both a future projection and absolute language unsupported by the 15-year record.
explanations.E: Too strong. The stimulus describes colonization of one transitional zone, not a trend across all zones. 'Eventually dominate all zones' overclaims both the scope and the trajectory of the observed changes.
